chunks: With this chain, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from his father, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
One who recites Surah al-A'raf every month will be among those for whom there is no fear nor sorrow on the Day of Judgment.
If he recites it every Friday, he will be among those who are not held to account on the Day of Judgment.
Know that within it is a Muhkam (clear/definitive verse), so do not neglect its recitation, for it will bear witness on the Day of Judgment for whoever recites it.

key_terms.سُورَةَ الْأَعْرَافِ: Surah al-A'raf (The Heights), a chapter of the Quran
key_terms.لَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَن: No fear upon them nor will they grieve (Quranic phrase)
key_terms.لَا يُحَاسَبُ: Not held to account (exempt from strict reckoning)

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual benefits of reciting Surah al-A'raf monthly and on Fridays according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Compiled by Shaykh al-Saduq, this hadith underscores the immense spiritual merit of reciting Surah al-A'raf, linking consistent devotion to exemption from fear, sorrow, and strict accountability on the Day of Judgment. The mention of a 'Muhkam' (clear/unambiguous) verse serving as a witness highlights the Shia scholarly view that specific verses possess an intercessory quality, testifying on behalf of the faithful who engage with the Quran regularly.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. From the previous chain from al-Hassan b. Ali from his father from Abi Basir from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said: “
One who recites Surah Araaf once every month would be included among those for whom there is no fear or sorrow on the Day of Judgment.
One who recites it every Friday would be included among those for whom there is no accounting on the Day of Judgment.
Know that one of the Muhkamat (clear verses) of the Holy Quran is present in this Surah and it will bear witness on the Day of Judgment for the reciter.”
